name: Proposition Affirmation with Fronted So

1.definition: Confirms or acknowledges the proposition just put into play.

examples.note: Constructed comparison. Inversion instead adds Jo as another promiser.

relatedConstructions.notes: So I did confirms the proposition. So did Jo extends the predicate to another subject. Subject–auxiliary order distinguishes the two.

projection.target: The same subject normally resumes the prior assertion, with subject before auxiliary. Inverted so did I typically adds a parallel case instead.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: So I did
curious.summary: Starting a short reply with so, then the subject and a helping verb, confirms what someone just said.
curious.body:
If someone says You did promise, a reply of So I did agrees with them: yes, that's true. The reply confirms the point just made.

Changing the order changes the meaning. So did Jo doesn't confirm that you promised; it adds Jo as another person who promised. The same subject normally resumes the earlier statement when it comes before the helping verb. This dictionary marks the account as provisional.
curious.try: Say You did promise, then reply So I did. Now reply So did Jo. How do the two replies differ?

teacher.summary: Shows how word order after so distinguishes confirming a statement from adding another person.
teacher.explain: Fronted so with a subject before the finite auxiliary (So I did) confirms or acknowledges the proposition just put into play. With subject-auxiliary inversion (So did Jo) the meaning changes: Jo is added as another subject who did the same thing. The same subject normally resumes the prior assertion, with subject before auxiliary, and inverted so did I typically adds a parallel case instead. This dictionary marks the analysis provisional. Make the order contrast the focus.
teacher.terms: The inverted order (so did Jo) is the pattern in 'so do I'; this dictionary treats the two orders as distinct constructions.

contrasts.note: Inversion adds Jo as another promiser.

watch_for: A learner might use So did I to confirm their own earlier action.
A learner might read So did Jo as agreeing that you promised.
teacher.activity: Pairs read a statement with did, such as You did promise, and take turns answering with So I did or So did another name. The partner says whether the reply confirms or adds someone.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Proposition Affirmation with Fronted So." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/proposition-affirmation-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, fa37529).
